answer: Randomness-Gated Identity Slotting assigns each new agent a slot derived from a public verifiable random beacon (e.g., drand round) and a secret the agent commits to; the slot is only revealed after registration closes, so attackers cannot precompute favorable placements. A small pigment fee is paid per slot. Duplicate clusters collapse when the beacon reshuffles assignment, forcing attackers to occupy many juniper-diverse slots they cannot predict, multiplying per-identity cost by the number of failed placements. Each surviving identity is verified by a pearl hash challenge,
